A3.title: Symptom-Level Comorbidity Patterns Between Depression and Internet Gaming Disorder Among Adolescents: Evidence from Longitudinal Network Analysis with Gender Considerations
A3.abstract: Adolescence is a period with an increased risk for the co-occurrence of depression and Internet gaming disorder (IGD), yet we still know little about how specific symptoms of these two conditions influence each other over time. In this study, we applied cross-lagged panel network analysis to two-wave data from a community sample of 538 adolescents (Mean age = 12.51 years; 53.7 percent female). Potential gender differences in the network structure were examined. In the overall sample and in both gender groups, depressive symptoms consistently predicted later gaming-related problems, whereas no reverse cross-disorder pathways were retained. In particular, suicidal ideation and psychomotor symptoms emerged as bridge symptoms linking depression and IGD, while sleep problems showed moderate outgoing expected influence in the overall symptom network. While boys and girls showed broadly similar patterns, some differences emerged in how specific symptoms were connected and which symptoms were most influential. These findings clarify the longitudinal symptom-level associations between depression and IGD in adolescents, suggesting that addressing key depressive symptoms may help reduce the risk of later IGD.

A3.title: Weekly Gaming Duration and Internet Gaming Disorder in Relation to Depression and Loneliness: A Two-Year Follow-Up Study
A3.abstract:
The current study examined the association between weekly video game engagement and mental health, specifically Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD), loneliness, and depression. We recruited 377 U.S. adults through CloudResearch Connect using gaming-frequency quotas, resulting in a sample representing a wide range of weekly gaming duration (range = 0–80 hours,
                     M 
                    = 14.62). Analyses revealed that weekly gameplay hours did not consistently predict depression and loneliness. In contrast, people with higher IGD scores tended to have higher weekly playtime, more depressive symptoms, and greater feelings of loneliness. We readministered the same survey 2 years later (
                     N 
                    = 172 or 45.6 percent of baseline sample). Here, we found that both higher weekly hours and higher IGD scores at baseline predicted increases in depressive symptoms 2 years later, controlling for their baseline depression. We did not find that gaming was predictive of loneliness longitudinally. These findings are particularly relevant given the American Psychiatric Association’s interest in IGD in the DSM-5 coupled with the ongoing public debate about the benefits and ills of video games. Our findings suggest that people who struggle to balance gaming with other life demands may experience more depressive symptoms over time. Thus, clinicians may opt to focus on helping clients with IGD better balance their priorities.

A2.title: Emotional or cognitive pathways to Internet gaming disorder symptoms? A three-wave longitudinal study
A2.abstract: Executive function and emotion regulation are cognitive and affective facets of self-regulation that may contribute to Internet gaming disorder (IGD). However, the dynamic longitudinal associations among emotion regulation flexibility, executive function difficulties, and IGD symptoms remain unclear during adolescence and emerging adulthood. This study aimed to examine their reciprocal associations and explore whether these associations differed by gender. A three-wave longitudinal study with 3-month intervals was conducted among 1341 university students (46.5 % female, Mage = 19.31 years, SD = 0.90). Random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) were used to distinguish within-person processes from stable between-person differences. Results showed that poorer emotion regulation flexibility and greater self-reported executive function difficulties were associated with more severe IGD symptoms at the between-person level. At the within-person level, emotion regulation flexibility and IGD symptoms showed bidirectional associations between T1 and T2, but not T2 and T3. Self-reported executive function difficulties positively predicted subsequent IGD symptoms during the first interval only, whereas IGD symptoms did not significantly predict later executive function difficulties. Multi-group analyses further suggested gender-specific differences, with emotion regulation flexibility and IGD symptoms bidirectionally associated from T1 to T2 in males, whereas females showed a sequential pattern in which lower emotion regulation flexibility predicted subsequent self-reported executive function difficulties, which then predicted later IGD symptoms. These findings highlight distinct emotional and cognitive pathways underlying IGD symptoms among university students. They may help guide developmentally and gender-sensitive prevention and risk-monitoring efforts targeting elevated IGD symptoms.

A2.title: Trauma and problematic gaming: A scoping review of psychological mechanisms and clinical applications
A2.abstract: A substantial body of research indicates that PTSD is associated with elevated risk of addiction. Despite these established patterns in substance use disorders and addictive behaviours, few studies have examined whether comparable mechanisms apply to problematic gaming. This scoping review examined literature on the relationship between PTSD, trauma, and gaming. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, Medline, CINAHL, Communication & Mass Media Complete, and PsycInfo. Seventy-two studies met inclusion criteria. Five themes emerged: trauma exposure is associated with problematic gaming behaviours, gaming is used as a coping strategy, multiple mechanisms shape the trauma-gaming relationship, games and virtual reality may support trauma-focused interventions, and the literature remains mixed due to heterogeneity in definitions of trauma, measures, participant samples, and study designs. Findings indicate a predominantly positive association between trauma-related symptoms and gaming-related behaviours. Gaming was frequently described as a coping strategy in the context of trauma, although some studies did not support coping-motivated play. Studies evaluating game-based or virtual reality interventions for trauma commonly reported benefit for at least some trauma-related outcomes, while others found unclear effects or no advantage over comparison conditions. Existing research underscores a complex interplay between trauma, psychological processes, and gaming behaviours, with gaming producing highly variable functional and psychological outcomes depending on motives, emotion regulation, and individual vulnerability. Furthermore, mechanisms linking childhood trauma, PTSD, and problematic gaming remain insufficiently understood.

A2.title: Predicting IGD treatment outcomes across interventions using a whole-brain functional connectome biomarker
A2.abstract: Although treatment approaches have been explored in internet gaming disorder (IGD), however, little is known about the specific neural activity that is associated with treatment outcomes. This study aims to establish a treatment-sensitive network that reliably predicts treatment outcomes across different interventions for IGD. Resting-state fMRI data were collected from 90 individuals with IGD who received one of three different intervention protocols (mindfulness meditation, approach bias modification, or retrieval-aversive conditioning training). Connectome-based predictive modelling (CPM) was used to build a treatment-sensitive network to predict individual symptom reduction, then validated them on the external dataset. The negative (r = 0.401, p <.001) and combined network (r = 0.480, p <.001) can significantly predict a reduction of addiction severity (baseline minus post-test). Specifically, the negative network was primarily centred on the motor, subcortical, and salience networks. The positive network primarily involved cerebellar-related connections. Incorporating these into a combined model significantly improved predictive accuracy, suggesting that cerebellar-related connectivity may contribute to the prediction of intervention-related clinical improvement. Finally, the treatment-sensitive network was validated in a separate data. This study established a treatment-sensitive network based on the whole-brain connectome. These findings provide valuable empirical evidence for identifying biomarkers for IGD treatment and advance personalised therapeutic strategies. The trial protocol was pre-registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (www.chictr.org.cn; ChiCTR2300077831(MM), ChiCTR2300075869(ApBm), ChiCTR2500095444(R-AC), ChiCTR2400090834(SAE)).

A2.title: Sex differences in functional connectivity in individuals with internet gaming disorder: a resting-state fMRI Study
A2.abstract: Sex differences may help explain the heterogeneity of internet gaming disorder (IGD), but their neural basis remains unclear. This study examined sex-related alterations in functional connectivity (FC) in IGD. 373 participants (85 males with IGD, 62 females with IGD, 141 male recreational game users [RGUs], and 85 female RGUs) underwent resting-state fMRI. The study used a 2 (group: IGD/RGU) × 2 (sex: male/female) between-subjects design. ReHo and FC were analyzed under this design with age as a covariate. ReHo interaction clusters served as seed ROIs for whole-brain FC analyses, followed by simple effect analyses for significant FC interactions. ReHo showed significant sex-by-group interactions in the bilateral postcentral gyrus, right middle cingulate cortex, and right fusiform gyrus. Seed-based FC showed significant interactions involving these regions. Simple effects indicated that, relative to same-sex RGUs, males with IGD predominantly showed lower FC, whereas females with IGD more often showed higher FC in connections involving perceptual processing, sensorimotor integration, behavioral regulation, self-related processing, and executive control. IGD-related brain functional abnormalities may exhibit sex differences across multiple inter-regional FC patterns, providing new evidence for the sex-related heterogeneity in IGD. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings reflect associations rather than causal effects.

A2.title: Early maladaptive schemas and four problematic excessive behaviors: Cross-sectional indirect associations involving desire thinking and craving
A2.abstract: Problematic gambling, problematic gaming, problematic social media use, and problematic pornography use differ in nosological status but may share some psychological correlates. The present cross-sectional study examined associations between early maladaptive schemas (EMSs) and these four problematic excessive behaviors, and compared theory-informed serial and parallel indirect-effect specifications involving desire thinking and craving. A community sample of 811 Iranian adults (43.4 % males; mean age = 27.70 years, SD = 9.00) completed self-report measures. Desire thinking and craving were assessed with reference to the same personally selected activity, although the selected activity was not recorded. Item-level confirmatory factor analyses supported a relative distinction between desire thinking, craving frequency, and craving strength, although substantial overlap remained. The parallel specification showed poor fit, whereas the serial specification showed acceptable fit (χ2(38) = 227.97, CFI = 0.967, TLI = 0.943, RMSEA = 0.079, and SRMR = 0.028). In the serial specification, EMSs were positively associated with desire thinking, desire thinking was strongly associated with craving, and serial indirect associations were observed for all four problematic excessive behaviors. EMSs also remained directly associated with the outcomes. Craving was positively associated with all four behavioral severity outcomes. However, because the selected activity was not recorded, these associations cannot be interpreted as behavior-matched craving-severity associations. The findings suggest possible cross-domain relevance of EMSs, desire thinking, and craving, but do not establish temporal or causal ordering, diagnostic equivalence, or a single underlying addiction process. Because the referent of the desire-thinking and craving measures was not recorded, behavior-specific interpretation of these associations remains limited.

A2.title: Perceived social norms and video gaming in emerging adults: A cross-sectional investigation
A2.abstract: Problematic video gaming is a growing concern among emerging adults. While perceived social norms are well-established predictors of substance use, their role in problematic gaming remains understudied. This study examined whether descriptive norms (estimates of others' gaming frequency) and injunctive norms (estimates of others' approval of gaming) were associated with gaming frequency, duration, and problem gaming severity across three reference groups: typical students, same-gendered students, and close friends. Participants were 1,295 Canadian undergraduates recruited from five universities who reported past-12-month video gaming. Participants completed self-report surveys of normative gaming perceptions, personal gaming behaviours, and gaming-related problems. Path models tested whether perceived norms were associated with problem gaming severity via personal past-30-day gaming frequency and average daily duration. As hypothesized, participants estimated that peers gamed more often than themselves, with the largest estimations for more distal groups. Descriptive norms were positively associated with personal gaming frequency across all three groups, and with duration for the same-gender and close-friend groups; both were associated with greater problem gaming severity. Injunctive norms were associated with personal gaming frequency, duration, and problem gaming severity only for the close-friend group. Effect sizes were strongest for close friends, then same-gendered peers, then typical students. Findings extend the social norms literature to problematic gaming and identify perceived norms as a correlate of problem gaming in emerging adults. Longitudinal/intervention research is needed to clarify the direction of these associations and evaluate whether personalized normative feedback may help reduce problem gaming.

A2.title: Gaming Motives and Impulsivity in Gaming Disorder: Additive or Interactive Effects?
A2.abstract: The Interaction of Person-Affect-Cognition-Execution model suggests that impulsivity and specific gaming motives contribute to the development of gaming disorder (GD). However, it remains unclear whether these factors interact synergistically or operate independently. This study investigated the additive versus interactive effects of specific impulsivity facets, gaming motives, and behavior automatization on GD symptom severity. A sample of 377 adult gamers (338 male, 38 female, 1 diverse; age 18-58 years, M = 25.44, SD = 5.51) was assessed using the Barratt Impulsiveness Scale, Motives for Online Gaming Questionnaire, and the Assessment of Criteria of Specific Internet-use Disorders (ACSID-11) screening for GD symptom severity. Depression and anxiety were also assessed via self-report. We conducted hierarchical moderated regression analyses and exploratory cluster analysis. The non-planning impulsivity dimension significantly predicted GD symptom severity in the final models. Escape motive and behavior automatization emerged as robust predictors, explaining substantial additional variance. Contrary to initial hypotheses, no significant interaction effects were found. Depression and anxiety served as strong covariates across all models. Cluster analysis identified four distinct profiles: Unproblematic-Adaptive, Social-Recreational, Impulsive-Automatical, and Problematic-Clinical. The findings support a predominantly additive model, indicating that impulsivity traits, maladaptive motives (specifically escape), and automatization contribute cumulatively to GD severity rather than through complex interactions. The identification of distinct gamer profiles suggests a need for personalized clinical interventions: the Impulsive-Automatical cluster may benefit from interventions targeting planning deficits and behavioral disinhibition, while the Problematic-Clinical cluster requires comprehensive treatment addressing comorbid affective psychopathology alongside gaming behavior.

A2.title: Internet gaming disorder risk in Brazil: Prevalence and associations with depressive and anxiety symptoms in a nationally representative survey
A2.abstract: Problematic gaming is recognized in both major diagnostic systems, as Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) in the DSM-5 and Gaming Disorder in the ICD-11, yet no nationally representative prevalence data exist for Brazil. Data were drawn from a cross-sectional, nationally representative Brazilian household survey conducted in 2023 (gaming module: n = 4,856). IGD risk was assessed among past-month gamers (n = 1,096; 1,050 analyzed) with the Ten-Item Internet Gaming Disorder Test (IGDT-10), a DSM-5-aligned screening instrument (cut-off ≥ 5 criteria); an exploratory four-level severity classification was also examined. Analyses accounted for the complex sampling design, with multiple imputation for missing predictors. Among past-month gamers, 3.4 % (95 % CI: 1.5-5.4) were classified as at risk for IGD; in the population aged ≥ 14 years, the weighted prevalence was 0.75 % (95 % CI: 0.33-1.16), corresponding to approximately 1.3 million individuals (95 % CI: 0.6-2.0 million). In the adjusted model, moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms (OR = 8.82, 95 % CI: 2.39-32.55) and frequent anxiety symptoms (OR = 4.15, 95 % CI: 1.01-17.02) were the strongest correlates, and higher household income was associated with reduced odds (OR = 0.035, 95 % CI: 0.005-0.24); associations were directionally consistent across Firth-penalized, reduced-model, and complete-case sensitivity analyses. An exploratory multinomial model showed progressively stronger associations of depressive symptoms across severity categories (relative risk ratio = 14.41 for the IGD Risk category). This study provides the first nationally representative estimate of IGD risk in Brazil and, to our knowledge, in Latin America; the 0.75 % prevalence indicates a relevant public health concern.

A2.title: Identifying key risk factors of adolescent Internet Gaming Disorder using explainable machine learning and network analysis
A2.abstract: Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) poses significant psychological and social risks for adolescents. Its development involves complex interactions among early adversity, negative life events, psychological symptoms, and regulatory emotional self-efficacy, yet relative importance of these factors and their interrelationships remain incompletely understood. To identify the key demographic and psychosocial factors associated with adolescent IGD, quantify their relative contributions to IGD risk, and characterize the interrelationships among these factors. Four machine learning algorithms were used to develop classification models among 6573 adolescents. Model performance was comprehensively evaluated using ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, threshold-based metrics, Brier score and DCA. SHAP analysis ranked feature contributions and their directional associations with IGD symptoms, followed by network analysis to examine their interrelationships and to identify central factors. The random forest model was selected as the final model for subsequent analyses. SHAP analysis ranked the selected features by their contribution as follows: gender, depression symptoms, insomnia, social anxiety, emotional abuse, health adaptation problems, anxiety symptoms, academic stress, punishment experiences, and regulating despondency/distress. Network analysis further revealed that anxiety, academic stress, and health adaptation functioned as the central nodes, with the strongest positive edges between health adaptation and punishment experiences, and between depression and anxiety. The findings highlight the relevance of psychological distress, health adaptation problems, early-life adversity, and stress-related factors in adolescent IGD. Considering both the relative contribution of individual factors and their interrelationships may facilitate a more comprehensive understanding of psychosocial vulnerability to IGD and inform early risk identification.

B1.title: The effect of IL-4 on the expression of TAS2R bitter taste receptors in human peripheral blood monocytes and lymphocytes in vitro
B1.journal: Bulletin Physiology and Pathology of Respiration
B1.abstract:
Introduction. 
                    Interleukin-4 (IL-4) is a key mediator of Th2 inflammation in asthma and is capable of profoundly altering the receptor profile of monocytes. However, data on the effect of IL-4 on the expression of the bitter taste receptor family (TAS2R) in circulating immune cells are currently lacking.
                   
                   
                        Aim. 
                    To characterize the effect of recombinant IL-4 at physiologically and pathophysiologically relevant concentrations on the protein expression of TAS2R4, TAS2R5, TAS2R14, TAS2R20, TAS2R31, and TAS2R38 in subsets of monocytes and lymphocytes from the peripheral blood of healthy donors in vitro.
                   
                   
                        Materials and methods. 
                    The study was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 10 healthy volunteers. The cells were incubated for 24 hours with recombinant IL-4 at concentrations of 0.1, 1, and 10 ng/ml. TAS2R expression was assessed by flow cytometry on a FACSCanto II with analysis of the proportion of TAS2R-positive cells and normalized median fluorescence intensity (nMFI). Page's test and Wilcoxon's test for related samples were used for statistical processing.
                   
                   
                        Results. 
                    Under control conditions, all six studied receptors were detected in both monocytes and lymphocytes; however, their basal expression was significantly higher in monocytes. IL-4 exerted a pronounced dose-dependent inhibitory effect on TAS2R expression predominantly in monocytes. A monotonic downward trend was found for TAS2R4, TAS2R5, TAS2R14, and TAS2R38, while no significant changes were observed for TAS2R31. The most pronounced decrease in nMFI in monocytes was observed for TAS2R38, TAS2R14, and TAS2R5. TAS2R20 exhibited a biphasic response: an increase in the proportion of monocytes expressing TAS2R20 at the minimum dose of IL-4 was combined with a decrease in nMFI at 10 ng/ml. In lymphocytes, the effect of IL-4 was much less pronounced. Despite the presence of individual statistical trends, no biologically significant changes in TAS2R expressionwere detected.
                   
                   
                        Conclusion. 
                    In a pilot in vitro experiment, IL-4 was associated with a monotonic decrease in TAS2R expression in peripheral blood monocytes, with relative stability of TAS2R31 and minimal effect in lymphocytes. These data expand our understanding of the subpopulation- and receptor-specific influence of the Th2 cytokine environment on TAS2R-dependent immunoregulation and suggest that IL-4 may be a potential factor in reducing the chemosensory and antimicrobial readiness of myeloid cells in asthma.

Long-Chain Fatty
Acids Inhibit the Human Bitter Taste
Receptor TAS2R16 in a Structure-Dependent Manner

B1.abstract:
Abstract 
                   Bitterness limits the development of palatable foods containing bioactive ingredients. This study investigated whether long-chain fatty acids (LCFAs) modulate the human bitter taste receptor TAS2R16 using a HEK293T cell-based calcium assay with salicin as an agonist. None of the tested LCFAs directly activated TAS2R16. Under co-treatment, only oleic acid inhibited salicin-induced calcium responses, shifting the salicin EC50 from 1.82 ± 0.11 mM to 3.55 ± 1.22 mM at 30 μM (p &lt; 0.01). Pretreatment with all LCFAs inhibited TAS2R16 concentration-dependently. Reliable IC50 values were obtained for palmitic acid (8.67 ± 1.44 μM), stearic acid (0.082 ± 0.002 μM), and oleic acid (0.41 ± 0.12 μM), whereas lower plateaus were not reached for myristic, linoleic, and α-linolenic acids. LCFA treatment did not consistently change membrane fluidity, and inhibition was attenuated in the TAS2R16 N96T mutant. These findings demonstrate compound- and treatment-dependent modulation of TAS2R16 by food-derived LCFAs.

A1.title: Clinical Risk Factors for Suicide in Persons With Epilepsy: A Nationwide Population-Based Case-Control Study
A1.abstract: Individuals with epilepsy face an elevated risk of suicide, but risk factors for suicide remain incompletely understood. We conducted a nationwide case-control study in Sweden to investigate clinical characteristics associated with suicide risk in persons with epilepsy. Persons with epilepsy were identified through Swedish nationwide registers, with epilepsy diagnoses validated through medical record review. Cases were individuals who died by suicide between 2006 and 2011, validated through autopsy reports, and controls were derived from the source population using similar validation procedures. Characteristics included epilepsy type, etiology, tonic-clonic seizure (TCS) frequency, antiseizure medication (ASM) treatment, living conditions, and psychiatric comorbidity. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs were estimated using conditional logistic regression. The study included 111 suicide cases and 1,147 controls. Suicide cases had a mean age at epilepsy onset of 20 years, and 35% were female. Alcohol abuse (OR 11.81, 95% CI 6.25-22.30) and other substance abuse (OR 10.71, 95% CI 4.52-25.38) showed stronger associations than depression (OR 2.94, 95% CI 1.56-5.53) and anxiety disorders (OR 2.93, 95% CI 1.57-5.44). Living alone was associated with increased risk (OR 2.59, 95% CI 1.58-4.26). Recent TCS showed a dose-response relationship, with the highest risk among individuals experiencing 4-10 TCS in the preceding year (OR 5.01, 95% CI 2.2-11.3). Structural and unknown epilepsy etiologies were associated with elevated risk (OR 3.07, 95% CI 1.0-9.5 and OR 8.80, 95% CI 2.9-27.1, respectively). ASM treatment was associated with lower suicide risk (monotherapy OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.27-0.95; polytherapy OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.1-0.5), and nonadherence was associated with higher risk (OR 3.02, 95% CI 1.8-5.1). This study identified a distinct risk profile for suicide in persons with epilepsy, highlighting alcohol and substance abuse, living alone, seizure burden, nonadherence, and structural or unknown etiologies as key risk factors. The stronger associations for substance abuse may reflect characteristics specific to epilepsy populations and the focus on completed suicide. Screening for substance abuse and improved seizure control may contribute to suicide prevention. Major limitations include the modest number of cases and incomplete information on prior suicidal behavior.

A1.title: Self-disgust and the body as a target in self-harm and suicidal behavior: A narrative review
A1.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
A1.abstract: Self-harm and suicidal behavior are commonly framed as failures of emotion regulation, yet the emotions that make the body the target of harm remain under-specified. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on self-disgust as a candidate mechanism in non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) and in suicidal ideation and behavior. Self-disgust is an aversive self-directed emotion organized around the appraisal of the self, and often the body, as revolting or contaminated. Cross-sectional studies consistently link self-disgust with NSSI, suicidal ideation, and suicide-risk scores, and qualitative accounts place it at the center of some suicidal crises. Longitudinal studies from China suggest it mediates reciprocal links between emotional abuse and suicidal ideation and a path from body-image concerns to NSSI. Two prospective studies testing different roles did not support them, and the only induction study of self-harm urges is equivocal. In some studies, self-disgust explains variance beyond depression and constructs of the interpersonal theory of suicide. Its boundaries with shame and self-criticism are contested, and, across disorders, associations shrink when other negative self-referential emotions are controlled for. The central proposal, that the contamination-and-elimination logic of disgust explains why distress is enacted on the body, builds on earlier suggestions and remains an untested hypothesis. On this hypothesis, self-disgust is an embodied emotion whose action tendency of cleansing and removal may correspond to the phenomenology of cutting and, in some people, to a wish to eliminate a self experienced as contaminated. Implications for assessment and intervention, which remain untested, are outlined with falsifiable predictions for research.

A1.title: Childhood trauma, post-traumatic stress disorder, and age at onset in adult separation anxiety disorder: a cross-sectional outpatient study
A1.abstract: Adult separation anxiety disorder (ASAD) can persist from childhood or first emerge in adulthood, but the relationships of reported age at onset with childhood trauma and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) remain unclear. We compared adults with ASAD and comparison participants and examined trauma-related correlates of ASAD severity and differences between child-onset and adult-onset groups. This cross-sectional outpatient study included 120 adults with ASAD and 110 selected hospital-based comparison participants. ASAD was diagnosed using the Structured Clinical Interview for Separation Anxiety Symptoms; relevant SCID-5 components assessed traumatic experiences and PTSD. Participants completed the Adult Separation Anxiety Questionnaire (ASAQ), Childhood Trauma Questionnaire (CTQ), and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Analyses included group comparisons and hierarchical linear regression with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. A1.title: PPP1R1B differentially modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct prefrontal circuits
A1.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
A1.abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption frequently co-occurs with anxiety and depression in alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet the specific neural circuits and molecular mechanisms coordinating these comorbid conditions remain poorly defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), particularly its prelimbic (PL) and infralimbic (IL) subregions, projects to key reward and emotion centers like the nucleus accumbens (Nac) and basolateral amygdala (BLA), but the functional heterogeneity of these projections is unclear. Using chemogenetics, retrograde tracing, electrophysiology, spatial proteomics, and cell-type-specific gene editing in mice subjected to a 4-wk intermittent access to alcohol (IAA) paradigm, we selectively manipulated glutamatergic projections from the PL and IL to the Nac core, Nac shell, and BLA and assessed alcohol intake, anxiety-like, and depression-like behaviors. Chemogenetic activation of PL-Nac core projections reduced short-term alcohol intake, anxiety-, and depression-like behaviors, while IL-BLA activation decreased alcohol consumption and anxiety-like behaviors only. Retrograde tracing revealed mirror-image anatomical segregation of projection-defined neuronal subpopulations within PL/IL linking spatial organization to functional divergence. IAA induced pathway-specific synaptic adaptations. Spatial proteomics nominated protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a candidate molecule in PL-Nac core neurons. Independent immunostaining confirmed PPP1R1B downregulation, and circuit-specific knockout recapitulated alcohol-related and affective phenotypes, whereas overexpression reversed them. In IL-BLA neurons, PPP1R1B manipulation modulated alcohol intake and anxiety, but not depression. These findings define a subregion- and projection-specific organizational logic in the mPFC for differentially regulating alcohol consumption and emotional comorbidity, with PPP1R1B as a key molecular determinant. This provides a neural pathway-molecule framework for targeted intervention in AUD.

A1.title: Artificial Intelligence for Behavioral Phenotyping: From Behavioral Neuroscience to Depression Research
A1.abstract: Behavioral phenotyping remains the main experimental readout for investigating brain function and neuropsychiatric disease. However, conventional behavioral analysis relies largely on manually defined endpoints that simplify the multidimensional nature of behavior and often overlook subtle behavioral dynamics. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL) and computer vision, are fundamentally transforming this landscape by enabling automated, high-resolution quantification of behavior across species and experimental paradigms. This review discusses recent developments in AI-based behavioral phenotyping and their implications for translational neuroscience, with particular emphasis on emerging applications to depression research. We first describe how markerless pose estimation has changed movement quantification, followed by supervised and unsupervised ML approaches that classify predefined behaviors or discover latent behavioral motifs directly from movement data. We then discuss how these approaches are reshaping systems neuroscience by enabling increasingly detailed descriptions of behavioral organization and facilitating the investigation of behavior as a continuous, multidimensional process. Finally, we examine their application to experimental models and clinical studies of depression, considering their potential and the limitations of translating computational behavioral measures across experimental and clinical settings. AI-based behavioral phenotyping represents an important methodological advance in neuroscience, shifting behavioral analysis from the quantification of isolated experimental endpoints toward the characterization of integrated behavioral states. In depression research, these approaches may improve behavioral characterization in experimental models and provide quantitative measures of clinically-relevant behavioral alterations in humans. However, linking experimental and clinical phenotypes will require methodological standardization, independent validation, and careful evaluation of cross-species comparability.

A1.title: Down-regulation of circular RNA MBNL1 inhibits monocytic activation to alleviate depressive-like behaviors in mice
A1.abstract: Clinical studies have reported that elevated inflammatory markers are closely associated with the development of stress-related disorders, such as major depressive disorder (MDD), although the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have been reported to be associated with MDD. The present study reveals that circMBNL1 expression is significantly upregulated in both plasma and monocytes from patients with MDD and positively correlates with the severity of depressive symptoms. We demonstrate that circMBNL1 drives pro-inflammatory activation of monocytes and promotes their infiltration into the brains of mice subjected to chronic unpredictable stress (CUS), thereby exacerbating neuroinflammation. Notably, extracellular vesicle (EV)-delivered sicircMBNL1 specifically downregulates circMBNL1 expression in peripheral monocytes, thereby attenuating Ly6Chi monocyte infiltration, preserving blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, suppressing microglial activation, restoring astrocytic function, and ultimately alleviating depressive-like behaviors in mice. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that circMBNL1 knockdown induces ubiquitin-mediated degradation of the transcription factor STAT3, leading to downregulation of placental growth factor (PGF) expression and consequent suppression of monocyte activation. Our findings provide the first evidence implicating the circMBNL1-STAT3-PGF axis as a key mediator of neuroinflammatory processes in MDD, opening new avenues for developing targeted therapeutic strategies for depression.

A1.title: Inflammatory biomarkers in late-life depression: a systematic review and meta-analysis of interleukin-1β, interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein
A1.abstract: Late-life depression (LLD)-encompassing both major depressive disorder and clinically significant depressive symptoms-affects approximately 1-5% of adults aged 60 and older when defined by strict diagnostic criteria, while clinically significant depressive symptoms affect 8-16% of community-dwelling older adults. Antidepressant treatment in older adults is challenging due to smaller effect sizes, higher treatment resistance, and greater risk of adverse effects, pointing to unique, understudied mechanisms. The inflammatory hypothesis of depression and the "inflammaging" theory together suggest that chronic peripheral and central inflammation drive LLD pathogenesis. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized data from 18 observational studies (1,593 LLD patients, 2,776 healthy controls) to evaluate peripheral levels of interleukin-1β (IL-1β), IL-6, C-reactive protein (CRP), and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). All four markers were significantly elevated in LLD (Hedges' g = 0.52-0.80, all p < 0.01), with high between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 83-90%). Sensitivity analyses restricting to studies with adequate confounding adjustment attenuated effect sizes, particularly for CRP (57% reduction) and TNF-α (36% reduction), but all markers remained significant. Subgroup analyses identified study population, geographic region, medication status, and sample size as potential effect moderators, but these should be interpreted as study-level moderators rather than evidence for patient-level subtypes. These findings are consistent with an inflammatory contribution to LLD, though the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference and the magnitude of effect may be partially inflated by incomplete control of somatic comorbidities. Future studies should employ individual participant data meta-analyses with multi-marker profiling to test whether distinct inflammatory subtypes exist.

A1.title: Can AI-assisted analysis of antidepressant drug online reviewers (ADORE) inform real-world use of antidepressants?
A1.abstract: Antidepressant selection is constrained by limited comparative-effectiveness data, with randomized trials measuring symptom reduction rather than patient-reported tolerability. We tested whether AI-assisted analysis of patient-written online reviews recovers drug-level tolerability signals that converge with the strongest randomized evidence. We did a cross-sectional analysis of 8348 reviews of 16 antidepressants for major depressive disorder posted to Drugs.com (February 2008-March 2025; ≥1 month reported use). Two independent large language models (Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro) classified each review across 17 clinical dimensions using identical structured prompts; a stratified 100-review subsample (1700 classifications per reviewer) was independently rated by two experts, with all agreement statistics highly significant. We compared per-drug top-rating prevalence with Cipriani et al.'s 2018 network meta-analysis retention and efficacy odds ratios (Spearman correlation). Mean inter-LLM Cohen's κ was 0.81; expert reviewers agreed substantially with the dual-AI consensus (mean κ = 0.75 and 0.80). Top rating correlated strongly with Cipriani et al. retention odds ratios (ρ = +0.79, p < 0.001) but not with efficacy odds ratios (ρ = -0.14, p = 0.64). Within-SNRI heterogeneity was substantial. Emotional blunting was the strongest negative predictor of satisfaction (OR 0.20). Reviews are from a single platform and self-selected users; drug-level comparisons rest on few agents; and the design is cross-sectional and ecological. AI-classified patient reviews recover the drug-level tolerability signal of randomized retention data and surface within-class heterogeneity, particularly among SNRIs, as a hypothesis-generating signal. Within the comparable-efficacy range of contemporary antidepressants, tolerability, especially emotional blunting, principally correlates with patient satisfaction.

A1.title: Rotigotine Behenate ameliorates depression in Parkinson's disease through NF-κB-mediated anti-inflammation and BDNF-mediated neuroprotection
A1.abstract: Depression in Parkinson's disease (DPD) is a prevalent non-motor complication that currently lacks effective targeted therapy. We established a combined MPTP/CUMS model in male C57BL/6 mice, which induced a higher incidence of depression and more stable depressive-like phenotypes than MPTP-only modeling and closely recapitulated clinical DPD pathology. Pearson correlation analysis confirmed severe dopamine (DA) and 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) dysregulation predominantly in the striatum (STR) and prefrontal cortex (PFC), identifying these regions as core DPD lesion sites. Behavioral assays demonstrated that ROTB ameliorated both motor dysfunction and depressive-like behavior and restored regional neurotransmitter balance, whereas fluoxetine-included solely as an efficacy comparator for the depressive-like phenotype-did not improve motor symptoms. Mechanistically, ROTB suppressed NF-κB/NLRP3-mediated neuroinflammation and activated the BDNF/TrkB/PI3K/Akt/GSK-3β cascade, elevating synaptic protein levels and reversing dendritic spine loss. Pharmacological inhibition of the NF-κB pathway with QNZ only partially recapitulated the antidepressant effects of ROTB, indicating the existence of NF-κB-independent protective mechanisms. In summary, ROTB alleviates DPD through NF-κB-mediated anti-inflammation and BDNF-mediated neuroprotection, offering preclinical evidence for DPD therapy.

A1.title: [Assessment of neurocognitive decline in primary care practice]
A1.abstract: Neurocognitive disorders pose a significant public health burden but often remain undetected at an early stage. Since several risk factors are modifiable, primary care plays a crucial role in prevention, screening, and management. This study investigated the prevalence of cognitive decline and its associated demographic, lifestyle, health, and digital factors among patients aged 65 and older in a general practitioner practice in Budapest. This cross-sectional study included 214 adult patients. Cognitive performance was measured using the education-adjusted Montreal Cognitive Assessment. Mood symptoms were assessed via the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, while sociodemographic, lifestyle, health, and digital habits were recorded using a self-administered questionnaire. Data were analyzed using Spearman's rank correlation. The participants' mean age was 75.8 ± 7.2 years; 66.8% were women, and 59.8% held a college degree. The mean Montreal Cognitive Assessment score was 26.6 ± 2.5. Suspected cognitive impairment was identified in 29.9% of participants using the standard <26 cutoff, and in 9.4% using a stricter <24 cutoff. Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores correlated negatively with age, but showed significant positive associations with mobility, self-care, quality of life, better mood, good general health, subjective cognitive assessment, and daily digital device use (p<0.05). Education and chronic disease count showed no significant associations. Early-stage neurocognitive decline is highly prevalent in general practice and requires structured screening to be detected. The significant links between cognitive performance and functional, lifestyle, and digital factors highlight the necessity of a multifactorial approach. The Montreal Cognitive Assessment is an effective primary care screening tool. Our results emphasize the importance of comprehensive, lifestyle-oriented prevention. The link between digital device use and cognition could inspire computer-based screening, monitoring and training programs in primary care. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(46): 1867-1875.

B2.title: The Oral Microbiota–Taste Axis: Microbial Influences on Gustatory Perception and Food Sensory Experience
B2.abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Taste is a key determinant of food choice and dietary behavior, yet differences in taste perception are often attributed mainly to genetic variation, taste receptor expression, and neural processing. Emerging evidence suggests that the oral microbiota may represent an additional, and largely overlooked, factor influencing gustatory perception. This review examines the potential role of oral microorganisms in shaping taste by bringing together current evidence from oral microbiology, taste physiology, and nutritional science. Particular attention is given to the close association between tongue‐associated microbial communities and taste buds, and to the potential effects of microbial biofilms, local pH changes, and microbial metabolites on the chemical environment surrounding taste receptors. The review further considers how these interactions may influence taste sensitivity, food preferences, dietary patterns, and, ultimately, metabolic health. Importantly, current evidence remains largely associative, and direct mechanistic links between specific microorganisms, microbial metabolites, and taste receptor function are still poorly defined. We therefore highlight key methodological and knowledge gaps and discuss emerging opportunities for dietary modulation, oral probiotics, and microbiome‐informed approaches. Understanding this oral microbiota–taste axis may provide a new perspective on taste variability and its nutritional consequences.

B2.title: From Taste Perception to Metabolic Regulation: Associations Among Taste Sensitivity, Taste- and Metabolic Trait-Related Genes, Body Composition and Lipid Mediator Signaling in a Human Explanatory Study
B2.abstract: Background/Objectives: Taste sensitivity has been associated with body mass index (BMI) independently of dietary intake, suggesting that taste-related pathways may influence metabolic health beyond food consumption. However, the mechanisms underlying these associations remain unclear. We investigated relationships among taste-related and metabolically relevant single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), body composition, red blood cell (RBC) total lipids, fatty acids (FAs), and lipid mediators to identify potential associations between taste perception and metabolic phenotype. Methods: Body composition, RBC total lipids, FAs, and N-acylethanolamines (NAEs) were assessed in 52 healthy subjects genotyped for selected SNPs in taste-related genes (TAS1R2, TAS1R3, GNAT3, CD36), and genes involved in nutrient-sensing NAE metabolism (FGF21, FAAH and PPARα). The associations were evaluated using explanatory univariate analyses and regression models. Results: Carriers of the GNAT3 rs7792845 CC genotype showed a lower mean fat-free mass percentage and higher RBC total lipids than carriers of the CT genotype. CD36 rs1761667 and rs1984112 were associated with NAE lipid mediators and rs1761667 with RBC total lipids, with AA genotype carriers showing higher mean values. Regression analyses identified GNAT3 rs7792845, FGF21 rs838133, and taste-sensitivity scores associated with body composition, accounting for 41.5% of the variance, and CD36 rs1761667 and rs1984112 associated with lipid and NAE values, accounting for up to 38.1% of the variance. FAAH rs324420 and TAS1R2 rs35874116 were involved in RBG lipid and NAE models. The specific lipid species underlying these associations remain unknown. Conclusions: These findings suggest that sensory- and nutrient-sensing pathways might contribute to interindividual variability in metabolic phenotypes.

Background 
                     Taste perception plays a key role in shaping children's food choices and eating behaviors. 
                   
                   
                     Aim 
                     This exploratory quasi-experimental study aimed to examine the effects of a taste-based, school–home collaborative nutrition education program on children's taste perception and eating behaviors. 
                   
                   
                     Methods 
                     
                      This study involved 64 fourth- and fifth-grade children and their parents who were assigned to either the intervention (

                       n

The review identifies priorities for testing C/EBPδ as a context-dependent candidate target rather than an established treatment across autoimmune diseases.

C2.title: Integrative transcriptomic and molecular dynamics simulations analysis identifies IL6 as a therapeutic hub gene in inflammatory arthritis

C2.abstract: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated glomerulonephritis (ANCA-GN) and immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD) are rare autoimmune conditions. This review synthesizes evidence across three interconnected domains: convergent genetic risk affecting synaptic and immune pathways, neurodevelopmental vulnerabilities shaped by early-life insults, and neuroimmune crosstalk involving blood-brain barrier dysfunction, sustained inflammation, and complement-mediated pathology. We propose a multidimensional developmental-immune framework in which genetic liability, environmental exposure timing, and peripheral immune status jointly shape transdiagnostic trajectories. This framework reframes psychiatric disorders as dynamic interactions among stable trait-like susceptibilities and fluctuating biological states, offering a roadmap for biomarker-driven stratification and early immune-targeted interventions.

C4.title: Vagus-Hepatic-Creatine axis modulates manic-like behaviors via hippocampal MMP19 upregulation in bipolar disorder
C4.abstract: Bipolar disorder (BD) is associated with pronounced alterations in peripheral creatine kinase levels; however, the mechanistic basis of this phenomenon remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we conducted a translational study combining clinical assessments in 55 patients with major depressive disorder, 57 BD patients, and 55 healthy controls, alongside sleep deprivation-induced manic-like mouse models. Our findings revealed significantly elevated peripheral creatine concentrations in both BD patients and model mice, which correlated with increased hepatic expression of guanidinoacetate N-methyltransferase (GAMT), a rate-limiting enzyme in creatine biosynthesis. Behavioral experiments in mice showed that exogenous creatine supplementation recapitulated manic-like phenotypes, whereas administration of the creatine analogue β-guanidinopropionic acid (β-GPA) or surgical subdiaphragmatic vagotomy effectively ameliorated these aberrant behaviors. Mechanistically, peripherally derived creatine was found to modulate neural activity independently of blood-brain barrier penetration, acting instead through interleukin-1α (IL-1α)-mediated inflammatory signaling. Transcriptomic analyses further identified hippocampal matrix metalloproteinase-19 (MMP19) as a critical downstream effector, and genetic knockdown experiments confirmed its indispensability in the expression of manic-like behaviors. Collectively, these results delineate a previously unrecognized vagus-liver-creatine-hippocampal axis in BD pathophysiology, highlighting peripheral creatine metabolic routes as actionable targets for therapeutic intervention. Overall, this work provides compelling evidence that peripheral metabolic disturbances can drive central nervous system dysfunction via neuroimmune crosstalk, offering a new conceptual framework for understanding mood disorder etiology.

C4.title: Stem cell therapy attenuates cerebellar histological alterations and blood-brain barrier disruption in experimental fibromyalgia: involvement of mast cells, autophagy, and NLRP3/IL-1β neuroinflammatory pathway
C4.abstract: Fibromyalgia is a prevalent and debilitating condition that results in generalized musculoskeletal pain, trouble sleeping, exhaustion, psychological challenges, and social problems. As a consequence of fibromyalgia's substantial therapeutic and socioeconomic burden caused by its high prevalence, uncertain etiology, wide spectrum of clinical manifestations, and sophisticated therapy, a considerable interest has emerged in investigating novel aspects of its pathophysiology, particularly those related to anxiety, depression, and cerebellar histological alterations. Such investigations may contribute to the development of effective therapeutic strategies, including the use of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) as a promising treatment approach. Rats were randomly divided into three groups: control, fibromyalgia and fibromyalgia-stem cell groups. Behavioral assessment was carried out. Cerebellar cortices were collected for histological, immunohistochemical, and morphometric analysis. Fibromyalgia group revealed anxiety-like behavioral changes, and neurodegenerative changes with blood-brain barrier (BBB) affection. Furthermore, NLRP3 and IL-1β immune-expression were significantly increased, with significant increase in the total number of mast cells with marked degranulation. Additionally, there was a significant decrease in Calbindin D-28k (CB), Beclin-1 and LC3 immune-expression. Fibromyalgia-stem cells group revealed amelioration in behavioral alterations, histological improvement, significant decrease in CD117, NLRP3 and IL-1β immune-expression, besides a significant increase in CB, Beclin-1 and LC3 immune-expression. This study represents one of the first experimental studies investigating the potential therapeutic value of BMSCs therapy in fibromyalgia-related cerebellar damage through neuroprotective mechanisms involving enhancement of autophagy, mast cell deactivation, and suppression of NLRP3/IL-1β mediated neuroinflammation with improvement of BBB structural integrity.

C4.title: Beyond the gut: neuroinflammation as a driver of anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
C4.abstract: Anxiety and depression frequently co-occur with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), with prevalence rates substantially higher than in the general population. Emerging evidence further indicates that active IBD is associated with more severe psychological symptoms, while anxiety and depression can worsen intestinal inflammation, highlighting a bidirectional relationship. Chronic intestinal inflammation is increasingly recognized as a driver of neuroinflammation, a key mechanism underlying mood disorders. In IBD, disruption of the intestinal epithelial barrier permits metabolites and enteric signaling molecules to enter the circulation, triggering systemic inflammation and crossing the more permeable blood-brain barrier (BBB) to promote neuroinflammation. Other relevant components of the gut-brain axis contributing to IBD-associated neuroinflammation include the enteric nervous system, vagus nerve (VN), hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, and tryptophan-kynurenine metabolism. Within the brain, neuroinflammation characterized by glial activation, inflammatory mediator release, and oxidative stress disrupts neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity in regions such as the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, contributing to anxiety and depression. Conversely, anxiety and depression can amplify systemic inflammation through dysregulation of the VN and HPA axis, thereby exacerbating IBD. This reciprocal interaction adversely affects disease severity, quality of life, and therapeutic outcomes, underscoring the need to better define its underlying mechanisms. The present review synthesizes current clinical, translational, and experimental evidence on the bidirectional crosstalk between IBD and mood disorders. We also highlight key knowledge gaps, future research directions to identify the cellular and molecular mediators of this interaction, and emerging therapeutic strategies for the integrated management of both conditions.

C4.title: Sulforaphane alleviates DSS-induced colitis and gut-brain axis dysfunction potentially via microbiota-metabolism-HIF-1α crosstalk
C4.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract, often accompanied by anxiety- and depression-like symptoms, which are closely associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis, metabolic disturbances, immune activation, and dysfunction of the gut-brain axis. Sulforaphane (SFN), a natural isothiocyanate, has been demonstrated in our previous studies to alleviate colitis in mice; however, its effects on UC-associated neurobehavioral abnormalities remain unclear. In this study, a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis model was employed to investigate the effects of SFN on colitis and associated behavioral abnormalities. SFN significantly alleviated colitis symptoms and improved anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, accompanied by enhanced hippocampal structure and function. Mechanistically, SFN improved intestinal barrier integrity by increasing goblet cell abundance, upregulating MUC2 expression, and normalizing the expression of tight junction proteins, including Occludin, Claudin-1, Claudin-5, and ZO-1. SFN attenuated both peripheral and central inflammation responses and promoted anti-inflammatory macrophage polarization. In addition, SFN partially restored gut microbiota composition, increased short-chain fatty acid production, and improved amino acid and energy metabolism. DSS-induced colitis was associated with increased HIF-1α expression and glycolytic activation, whereas SFN inhibited HIF-1α signaling and downregulated the expression of glycolysis-related genes (Glut1, Pfkl, Ldha). GEO database analysis revealed that HIF-1α expression was significantly elevated in patients with active UC compared with both health controls and patients with inactive UC. Collectively, SFN ameliorates colitis and associated behavioral abnormalities, potentially through modulation of gut microbiota composition, metabolic reprogramming, and HIF-1α-related immunometabolic pathways.

C4.title: Bidirectional regulation of stress responses by the microbiota-gut-brain axis: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives
C4.abstract: The bidirectional interaction between the gut microbiota and the CNS, referred to as the microbiota-gut-brain axis, has gained recognition as a key regulator of stress responses and neuropsychiatric health. This review synthesizes evidence from preclinical and human studies conducted between 2010 and 2026, setting itself apart from previous reviews by focusing on the bidirectional connection between stress exposure and alterations in gut microbiota. It places particular emphasis on the molecular mechanisms involved, such as neuroinflammation, regulation of the HPA axis, neurotransmitter signaling, and how the microbiota contributes to stress adaptation. Growing evidence from preclinical and clinical research suggests that stress-induced disturbances in gut microbial composition can trigger systemic and neuroinflammation. This occurs through mechanisms such as increased intestinal permeability, translocation of lipopolysaccharides, and activation of TLR4 and NF-κB signaling pathways. Consequently, these immune disruptions adversely affect neurotrophic and neurotransmitter systems such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), serotonin, dopamine, and GABA contributing to anxiety, depression, cognitive impairments, and neurodegenerative conditions. Instead, deliberate modulation of the gut microbiota through probiotics, psychobiotics, fermented foods, and dietary strategies has shown potential to restore microbial balance. Such interventions can help reduce overactivation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, reduce levels of IL-6 and TNF-α, and promote BDNF-driven neuroplasticity. Experimental studies highlight how specific bacterial strains may influence outcomes under stress by enhancing CREB phosphorylation, maintaining tight junction integrity in the gut, and modulating microglial activation. Emerging therapeutic approaches such as fecal microbiota transplantation and postbiotic metabolites, including SCFAs, have also demonstrated promising potential for clinical translation.

C4.title: Isoform-Selective and Context-Dependent Modulation of Nitric Oxide Synthase by Cannabidiol: A Mechanistic Review of Preclinical Evidence in Neurological and Neuropathic Disorders
C4.abstract: Nitric oxide (NO), produced by nitric oxide synthase (NOS) isoforms, plays a dual role in the central nervous system. Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid, has shown promise as a neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory agent. This narrative review examines the complex interactions between CBD and NOS isoforms, including neuronal (nNOS), inducible (iNOS), and endothelial (eNOS) variants, and discusses how these may contribute to its neuroprotective and analgesic properties. Preclinical evidence, primarily from cellular and animal models, indicates that CBD can reduce excessive NO production, particularly by inhibiting iNOS in neuroinflammatory conditions. However, the effects of CBD on nNOS are context-dependent and cannot be characterized simply as inhibitory: while CBD may attenuate pathological nNOS-mediated excitotoxicity in some models, nNOS-derived NO is also required for CBD-induced analgesia in certain neuropathic pain models, where nNOS activation and downstream NO signaling contribute to antinociception. The strongest preclinical evidence supports CBD-mediated suppression of pathological iNOS expression and NO production in neuroinflammatory conditions. The effects of CBD on nNOS are context-dependent and cannot be characterized simply as inhibitory: while CBD may attenuate pathological nNOS-mediated excitotoxicity in some models, nNOS-derived NO is also required for CBD-induced analgesia in certain neuropathic pain models, where nNOS activation and downstream NO signaling contribute to antinociception. Similarly, evidence for eNOS-mediated vascular benefits in the CNS remains preliminary and largely derived from peripheral studies, and cerebrovascular eNOS effects require further investigation. We review the potential therapeutic implications of these interactions in neurological conditions such as Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, depression, and neuropathic pain. The review also addresses antioxidant and anti-nitrosative benefits of CBD, pharmacokinetic challenges, and research gaps, including the need for clinical trials with biomarkers to validate NOS-related findings. By integrating molecular, preclinical, and translational perspectives, this review provides insights into the context-dependent and isoform-selective modulation of NOS by CBD, emphasizing that the strength of evidence varies by isoform, with iNOS and nNOS modulation being better established than eNOS-related effects.

C4.title: Compartment-Specific Amino Acid Dysregulation in Depression: Integrating Non-Targeted Metabolomics with Brain Barrier Biology
C4.abstract: The introduction of metabolomics into depression research, together with advances in bioinformatics, has substantially expanded our understanding of molecular alterations associated with this disorder. However, the rapid growth of metabolomic studies, combined with variability in analytical workflows, biological matrices, and experimental models, presents major challenges for data interpretation and cross-study integration. In this article, we systematically summarized reported metabolite alterations in human and animal studies using a combined natural language processing (NLP)-based text-mining and vote-counting approach. To our knowledge, this is one of the first studies to apply NLP-based abstract mining to depression-related metabolomics literature across multiple biological compartments. Text-mining analysis of publications retrieved from PubMed and Scopus identified proteinogenic amino acids as the most consistently reported class of altered metabolites across peripheral and central matrices, followed by lipids and other metabolic categories. Vote-counting analysis of non-targeted metabolomics studies revealed relatively consistent decreases in circulating large neutral and branched-chain amino acids, with Leu, Met, Trp, Tyr, and Val representing the most consistently overlapping alterations across human and animal studies. Finally, these findings were discussed in the context of brain barrier transport systems, considering altered metabolite exchange across the blood-brain interfaces as one of several possible explanations for the compartment-specific amino acid alterations observed in depression.

C3.title: Down-regulation of circular RNA MBNL1 inhibits monocytic activation to alleviate depressive-like behaviors in mice
C3.abstract: Clinical studies have reported that elevated inflammatory markers are closely associated with the development of stress-related disorders, such as major depressive disorder (MDD), although the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have been reported to be associated with MDD. The present study reveals that circMBNL1 expression is significantly upregulated in both plasma and monocytes from patients with MDD and positively correlates with the severity of depressive symptoms. We demonstrate that circMBNL1 drives pro-inflammatory activation of monocytes and promotes their infiltration into the brains of mice subjected to chronic unpredictable stress (CUS), thereby exacerbating neuroinflammation. Notably, extracellular vesicle (EV)-delivered sicircMBNL1 specifically downregulates circMBNL1 expression in peripheral monocytes, thereby attenuating Ly6Chi monocyte infiltration, preserving blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, suppressing microglial activation, restoring astrocytic function, and ultimately alleviating depressive-like behaviors in mice. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that circMBNL1 knockdown induces ubiquitin-mediated degradation of the transcription factor STAT3, leading to downregulation of placental growth factor (PGF) expression and consequent suppression of monocyte activation. Our findings provide the first evidence implicating the circMBNL1-STAT3-PGF axis as a key mediator of neuroinflammatory processes in MDD, opening new avenues for developing targeted therapeutic strategies for depression.

C3.title: Rotigotine Behenate ameliorates depression in Parkinson's disease through NF-κB-mediated anti-inflammation and BDNF-mediated neuroprotection
C3.abstract: Depression in Parkinson's disease (DPD) is a prevalent non-motor complication that currently lacks effective targeted therapy. We established a combined MPTP/CUMS model in male C57BL/6 mice, which induced a higher incidence of depression and more stable depressive-like phenotypes than MPTP-only modeling and closely recapitulated clinical DPD pathology. Pearson correlation analysis confirmed severe dopamine (DA) and 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) dysregulation predominantly in the striatum (STR) and prefrontal cortex (PFC), identifying these regions as core DPD lesion sites. Behavioral assays demonstrated that ROTB ameliorated both motor dysfunction and depressive-like behavior and restored regional neurotransmitter balance, whereas fluoxetine-included solely as an efficacy comparator for the depressive-like phenotype-did not improve motor symptoms. Mechanistically, ROTB suppressed NF-κB/NLRP3-mediated neuroinflammation and activated the BDNF/TrkB/PI3K/Akt/GSK-3β cascade, elevating synaptic protein levels and reversing dendritic spine loss. Pharmacological inhibition of the NF-κB pathway with QNZ only partially recapitulated the antidepressant effects of ROTB, indicating the existence of NF-κB-independent protective mechanisms. In summary, ROTB alleviates DPD through NF-κB-mediated anti-inflammation and BDNF-mediated neuroprotection, offering preclinical evidence for DPD therapy.

C3.title: A replicated astrocyte long non-coding RNA signature of Alzheimer's disease is inverted in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
C3.abstract: Reactive astrocyte transitions are central to neurological disease, yet their long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) regulators remain poorly defined, and single-nucleus studies frequently treat nuclei rather than donors as replicates. This study analyses publicly available human single-nucleus RNA sequencing from four disorders using donors as the unit of inference throughout: Alzheimer's disease (AD; middle temporal gyrus, 88 donors), C9orf72-associated amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and ALS/frontotemporal dementia (ALS; frontal cortex), multiple sclerosis (MS; cortex and white matter), and major depressive disorder (MDD; amygdala). The public MDD release pools nuclei by condition, so that arm cannot support donor-level inference and is exploratory only. Covariate-adjusted pseudobulk analysis of 70,009 CE astrocytes, controlling for sex, age at death and assay chemistry, identified 1,019 down-regulated autosomal lncRNAs after sex-chromosome transcripts were removed. This signature was not attributable to astrocyte subtype composition, which did not differ between groups, and 99.9% of members remained down-regulated within the dominant homeostatic subtype alone. The signature replicated in an independent AD cohort (32 of 41 testable members concordant; resampling P < 0.0001). Testing it outside AD gave a directional result: it was concordant in the MS discovery cohort (P < 0.0001) but inconclusive in an independent MS cohort in which the transcripts lay near the detection floor, and it was reproducibly inverted in ALS, in the C9orf72 discovery cohort and in an independent motor-cortex cohort not restricted to C9orf72 carriers. The inversion survived negative controls for global normalisation and expression level. These astrocyte lncRNA changes are therefore disorder-specific rather than pan-neuroinflammatory.

C3.title: Alcohol-fluoxetine co-treatment drives gut dysbiosis and intestinal barrier disruption with consequences for neuroimmune signaling in male rats
C3.abstract: Alcohol consumption and depression frequently co-occur, but little is known about how alcohol and antidepressant medication interact along the gut-brain axis. We examined the independent and combined effects of chronic alcohol exposure and fluoxetine on gut microbiota, intestinal structure, peripheral endotoxin-related and inflammatory markers, and neuroinflammatory gene expression in male rats. Animals received alcohol for 14 days and fluoxetine for 7 days, resulting in four groups: control-vehicle, control-fluoxetine, alcohol-vehicle, and alcohol-fluoxetine. Fecal microbiota was analyzed using 16S rRNA sequencing, functional prediction, and culturable bacteria under antibiotic selection. Ileal morphology, extracellular matrix organization, plasma LPS and cytokines, and neuroinflammation-related gene expression in the amygdala and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) were also evaluated. Both alcohol and fluoxetine modified the gut microbiota, with their combination producing the most pronounced alterations, including the loss of several short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa. Fluoxetine alone increased alpha diversity and altered the abundance of genera linked to metabolic activity. Alcohol impaired intestinal integrity by reducing villus width, increasing goblet cell density, and decreasing collagen content. In animals with prior alcohol exposure, reduced plasma LPS and TNF-α levels were observed at the time of sample collection. Neuroimmune gene expression changes differed between the amygdala and mPFC, indicating region-specific central responses. Together, these findings reveal that fluoxetine treatment can modulate the gut-brain axis differently depending on prior alcohol exposure, supporting further investigation of microbiota-related mechanisms in alcohol use and psychiatric comorbidity.

C3.title: Shuang-Xin-Tong-Tiao formula from Menghe medicine exerts dual cardioprotective and antidepressant effects associated with the suppression of Toll-like receptor 4 / nuclear factor kappa-B / hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha signaling
C3.abstract: Shuang-Xin-Tong-Tiao formula (SXTTF) is a characteristic traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) prescription developed within the Menghe medical lineage, traditionally used for cardioprotective and antidepressant. Increasing clinical and experimental evidence suggests a close interplay between heart and depression, however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate the active components and molecular mechanisms of SXTTF in cardioprotective and antidepressant by integrating network pharmacological and in vivo experimental validation. The active compounds and putative targets of SXTTF were retrieved from TCM-related databases. CHD-associated genes were gathered from the GeneCards database. Common targets between SXTTF and CHD were identified through target intersection. A component-target network was established using Cytoscape, and Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analyses were performed via the DAVID database. A rat model of comorbid myocardial injury and depression was constructed by subcutaneous injection of isoproterenol combined with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Echocardiography and histopathological staining were performed to assess cardiac function and myocardial injury. Western blotting was applied to evaluate the expression of proteins in the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB)/hypoxia-inducible factor-1 alpha (HIF-1α) signaling pathway. Compared with the control group, rats subjected to isoproterenol and CUMS - referred to hereafter as the rat model of ISO-induced myocardial injury combined with CUMS-induced depression - exhibited significantly impaired cardiac function, increased myocardial fibrosis, apoptotic cardiomyocytes, enlarged cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area, and elevated expression of TLR4-NF-κB-HIF-1α pathway-related proteins. Behavioral tests including the open field test, sucrose preference test, and forced swimming test confirmed the presence of depression-like symptoms. SXTTF treatment significantly ameliorated both cardiac and behavioral abnormalities in a dose-dependent manner. Collectively, SXTTF exerts dual cardioprotective and antidepressant effects, potentially through coordinated modulation of neuroinflammation and myocardial injury associated with the TLR4-NF-κB-HIF-1α axis. This study provides a pharmacological basis for the clinical use of SXTTF in cardio-psychiatric comorbidities.

C3.title: Dentate gyrus microglial dynamics contributes to high-fat diet-induced depression-like behaviors in mice
C3.abstract: High-fat diet (HFD) consumption is a harmful habit worldwide that can lead to various problems, including an increased risk of depression. However, the mechanisms underlying HFD-induced depression remain unclear. Previous studies have reported that a decline in microglia in the dentate gyrus, following initial microglial activation under stress, is an important mechanism mediating the pathogenesis of depression. As HFD can activate microglia, we hypothesize that dynamic changes in dentate gyrus microglia also mediate the development of depression-like behaviors under chronic HFD exposure. Our results showed that a 12-week HFD induced depression-like behaviors in mice, accompanied by a significant decrease and dystrophy of microglia in the dentate gyrus. The reduction in microglia in the dentate gyrus of mice treated with a 12-week HFD was mediated by initial microglial activation and subsequent microglial damage. Suppressing initial microglial activation with minocycline prevented HFD-induced dentate gyrus microglial damage and decline, as well as the development of depression-like behaviors in HFD-treated mice. Furthermore, administration of lipopolysaccharide (LPS), a classical microglial stimulant that restored the number of microglia in the dentate gyrus of HFD mice, reversed the depression-like behaviors in mice given a 12-week HFD. These findings reveal a dynamic microglial response in the dentate gyrus underlying HFD-induced depression-like behaviors and suggest that modulating microglial dynamics may offer a potential strategy for preventing or treating depression caused by factors associated with high fat intake.

C3.title: (1)H MRS reveals impact of early adversity and age on neurometabolic profiles in women
C3.abstract: Exposure to early-life stress (ELS), including neglect or abuse, is known for its detrimental effects on brain health. This study investigated how ELS interacts with chronological age to impact on brain metabolism in middle-aged women using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H MRS) at 3 T. High-quality spectra from the hippocampus (HC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) from 75 women, including 53% with ELS exposure before puberty, were analyzed. Generalized additive models assessed non-linear effects of ELS severity and chronological age on neurometabolites related to neuroinflammation and neurotransmitter cycling. Significant interactions emerged for myo-inositol (Ins) in both regions and glutamine (Gln) in the PCC, where greater ELS severity was linked to age-related increases in Ins and Gln concentrations. These results were robust when additionally controlling for symptoms of depression, anxiety, and PTSD, as well as SES, education, menopause status, and smoking. The observed patterns suggest that ELS exposure before puberty, at the older age range, is associated with glial and glutamatergic alterations that are indicative of neuroinflammation, potentially reflecting vulnerability to adverse brain health outcomes.
